messages.text: De Zerbi compares Williams-Barnett to Lamine Yamal - who is Spurs teen?

metadata.summary: Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi was not surprised by a dazzling full-debut display from “special” talent Luca Williams-Barnett and compared the 18-year-old to Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal after Saturday’s 2-0 win over Ipswich.
metadata.content: Luca Williams-Barnett: Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi compares teenager to Lamine Yamal after Ipswich heroics | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Luca Williams-Barnett: Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi compares teenager to Lamine Yamal after Ipswich heroics Tottenham teenager Luca Williams-Barnett starred in Spurs' 2-0 home win over Ipswich on his first start for club; the 18-year-old scored the opener and helped set up Dominic Solanke's goal; Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi hails "special" talent and compares him to Barcelona's Lamine Yamal Saturday 21 November 2026 22:42, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett bagged a goal on his first Premier League start for Spurs Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi was not surprised by a dazzling full-debut display from “special” talent Luca Williams-Barnett and compared the 18-year-old to Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal after Saturday’s 2-0 win over Ipswich. De Zerbi turned to the highly rated Spurs academy graduate after two bright cameos and he delivered, scoring on his first Premier League start after 15 minutes before a mazy run set up Dominic Solanke at the start of the second half. After Williams-Barnett made his senior debut at the age of 16 last season, the clamour for the teenager to play has only increased during a difficult last 12 months, and De Zerbi decided 10 days ago to include him in the starting line-up against Ipswich. messages.text: Nations Championship: France vs South Africa in final as England face NZ rematch

metadata.summary: South Africa will face France in the inaugural Nations Championship final at Allianz Stadium Twickenham on Sunday November 29, despite suffering back-to-back defeats.
metadata.content: Nations Championship fixtures: France to play South Africa in final as England face New Zealand rematch plus Ireland vs Australia | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nations Championship fixtures: France to play South Africa in final as England face New Zealand rematch plus Ireland vs Australia World Rugby's 12-team Nations Championship launched in 2026, uniting Six Nations sides, Rugby Championship teams, Fiji, Japan; tournament saw Tests in July, November before Finals Weekend at Twickenham Nov 27-29; France to face South Africa, England vs New Zealand, Ireland vs Australia Saturday 21 November 2026 22:29, UK Image: France will face South Africa at Allianz Stadium Twickenham for the right to be Nations Championship title winners South Africa will face France in the inaugural Nations Championship final at Allianz Stadium Twickenham on Sunday November 29, despite suffering back-to-back defeats. The last round of regular fixtures for the tournament saw South Africa suffer defeat to Ireland in Dublin, a week on from losing to France in Paris, but owing to New Zealand losing to England at Twickenham - and failing to pick up any bonus points - the Springboks still finished top of the southern hemisphere table. France defeated Argentina with a bonus point to confirm their place at the top of the northern hemisphere table ahead of England and Ireland. messages.text: How 'complacent' Arsenal unravelled at Newcastle - and their key lesson

metadata.summary: From "exceptional" to "complacent" - Arsenal's drop-off in the second half at Newcastle was extraordinary.
metadata.content: Arsenal escape with 2-2 draw at Newcastle after 'complacent' second half almost proves costly for defending champions | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Arsenal escape with 2-2 draw at Newcastle after 'complacent' second half almost proves costly for defending champions Arsenal were completely dominant in the first half at Newcastle but saw their 1-0 lead turn into a 2-1 deficit before Noni Madueke rescued a point against their re-energised hosts; Mikel Arteta called the result "two points dropped" and revealed key lesson required to take "next step" Peter Smith Senior Football Journalist @psmithXI Saturday 21 November 2026 21:19, UK Image: Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes challenged by Newcastle's Sean Steur (AP Photo/Ian Hodgson) From "exceptional" to "complacent" - Arsenal's drop-off in the second half at Newcastle was extraordinary. Noni Madueke's equaliser at least rescued a point, but after completely dominating the first half at St James' Park Mikel Arteta says his team have learnt a harsh lesson about the need to deliver a complete performance in the Premier League. Credit has to go to Newcastle, who were energised by Matthias Jaissle's triple substitution at half-time, with Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey and Anthony Elanga bringing intensity. Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw brought the goals. But the Premier League champions were their own worst enemy and, in the end, were fortunate to get away with their lead at the top of the table improved - for now

messages.text: Kim hangs on to lead at CME Group Tour Championship

metadata.summary: A Lim Kim held on to the lead, reduced to one shot, going into the final round of the CME Group Tour Championship.
metadata.content: LPGA Tour: A Lim Kim hangs on to lead at CME Group Tour Championship with Nelly Korda two shots back | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content LPGA Tour: A Lim Kim hangs on to lead at CME Group Tour Championship with Nelly Korda two shots back A Lim Kim's lead was reduced by two bogeys down the stretch including one on the 18th at the CME Group Tour Championship where she remains the leader, one shot ahead of Jeeno Thitikul and Yuri Yoshida; live coverage continues on Sunday from 6pm on Sky Sports+ Saturday 21 November 2026 23:17, UK Image: A Lim Kim is the leader going into the final round of the CME Group Tour Championship A Lim Kim held on to the lead, reduced to one shot, going into the final round of the CME Group Tour Championship. Kim made a pair of bogeys down the stretch on Saturday and had to settle for a three-under 69 at the season-ending event with $4m at stake and Nelly Korda suddenly very much in the mix. Kim holed a birdie putt off the fringe on the par-three 12th, added another birdie at the 13th and looked to be in control with a three-shot lead over two-time defending champion Jeeno Thitikul and Yuri Yoshida at a rain-soaked Tiburon Golf Club. Korda, who can qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame with her fifth win of the year, had a season-high nine birdies and pulled within two shots until a three-putt bogey from long range on the par-four 18th.
